title: Observed site groups raised model failure clustering by 1.4 to 2.3 percent in eight partial worm maps at failure probability 0.5
abstract: We tested whether chemical site groups change complete connection failures beyond pair counts. Eight public worm maps supplied a common panel of 141 cells with presynaptic records in every map. The model assumes independent site failures and complete shared loss at each site. At failure probability 0.5, observed groups gave 1.39 to 2.30 percent more companion failed outputs than the means of controls with the same source-target counts and site sizes. Each map had two chains of 200 draws. All observed primary values exceeded all retained controls. The expected number of failed outputs stayed fixed. At failure probability 0.1, the excess was 7.82 to 20.42 percent; at 0.9, it was 0.067 to 0.160 percent. Independent set-union calculations and small exhaustive checks passed. These are model results, not measured release failures. Partial coverage, unknown release dependence, one species, and controls without spatial constraints limit transfer. The package contains original code, aggregate results, hashes and retrieval steps. External raw data and record-level extracts are excluded.

display.caption: Model companion failures per failed output and excess over fixed-count control means. All sites have the stated failure probability. Each map is a different animal. Lines join map labels and do not estimate development within one animal.

citations.reason: Motivates site-group controls. No code, cell list or record table was reused. We test complete connection failures instead of input covariance.
Tests total contact-loss tails. Our endpoint tests complete output-connection failures and controls preserve all pair counts and site sizes.
